references.title: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, X. Shao, T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, Singmaster's conjecture in the interior of Pascal's triangle, Quart. J. Math. 73 (2022) 1137–1177
references.note: Proposition 1.9 (distance estimate): two solutions (n,m), (n',m') of C(n,m) = t in the left half have m' − m ≪_ε exp(log^{2/3+ε}(n+n')), and n' − n ≪_ε exp(log^{2/3+ε}(n+n')) when m, m' ≥ exp(log^{2/3+ε}(n+n')). Its deduction of Theorem 1.3 (§1.2, (1.10)) turns this, with (1.5) and (1.7), into m − m', n' − n ≪_{ε'} exp(O((log log t)^{1−ε'})) for solutions in the region exp(log^{2/3+ε} n) ≤ m ≤ n/2, for any ε' < ε/(2/3+ε).

summary: Known (2022), not formalised. This hole is the bound (1.10) in Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Shao–Tao–Teräväinen's deduction of their Theorem 1.3 from Proposition 1.9, with ε = 1/6 (region threshold exp((log n)^{5/6})) and the exponent 1 − ε' = 9/10 (ε' = 1/10 < 1/5); the implied constant inside the exponent is absorbed for large a by taking ε' smaller (3/20) in the paper's bound. The paper states (1.10) for any other region solution against the one with maximal m; the derivation bounds n and n' from the region condition and (1.5)/(1.7) separately and then applies Proposition 1.9, so it holds for any two region solutions. Proposition 1.9 is the paper's main work: non-Archimedean arguments via the equidistribution estimate Proposition 1.12 over random primes; nothing of it is in Mathlib.
